messages:
Maya R: Hey team — customer (acme-ops) seeing a spike of 429s during a deploy window. Says it started when their traffic hit a large burst from EU to US fallback. They report request-id `req_0a8f3b9c` and timestamps correlate to 2026-11-04T14:12:xxZ. Any quick checks?

Samir P: TL;DR probably regional capacity + fallback causing cross-region throttles. Can you paste the exact `x-rw-region` headers and any X-RateLimit-* we returned?

Maya R: Customer included a snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2026 14:12:07 GMT
x-rw-region: eu-west-1
x-rw-fallback-region: us-west-2
x-rw-request-id: req_0a8f3b9c
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 12
```

Jen C: Looks like eu-west pool hit quota and requests were routed to us-west but then hit cross-region egress throttles. We have a separate cross-region throughput guard that sits between routing and remote pool. Might be the guard trimmed concurrent handoffs.

Maya R: They also sent a minimal repro curl that spikes concurrency:

```
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" \
       -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1" \
       -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

Kai: Important: if fallback happens, we overlay two limits — source region's reserved capacity and the destination region's guard. If dest is under pressure, the router will 429 back with `x-rw-fallback-throttle` header. Do we see that in logs?

Maya R: Customer didn't get `x-rw-fallback-throttle` header, only the standard rate-limit. They said the 429 pages were inconsistent — some calls were fine, others 429 even with same payload.

Samir P: That fits transient routing races. If eu-west dequeues requests and attempts async reroute, some requests will enqueue in us-west pool which may already have a transient hot spot (evictions, GC on the host). We should ask for a sample request id list. Also check if their requests had `Prefer: low-latency` or pinned to high-throughput models.

Jen C: Actionable repro steps for support to run:
  1) Ask customer to run short burst at safe level: 100 concurrent for 90s against eu-west to reproduce (we avoid 300+ to not overload infra).
  2) Capture response headers for each request and include first/last 20 request ids.
  3) If possible, toggle region preference header to `auto` so we can see router behavior stats.
  4) Give us a time window +/- 5 minutes.

Maya R: I've asked them to run 100 concurrent. They pushed back; worried about causing outages. I told them we can coordinate with ops if they want to do a heavier test.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout id droll-927 at Thu Nov 04 14:15:10 UTC — affected service: router-v2

Kai: Ah — there’s the likely confounding factor. Router-v2 rollout started ~14:15 — if the customer burst overlapped the rollout we might see inconsistent routing rules while the new peers joined the mesh. That would explain mixed 429s.

Samir P: Good catch. Router rollouts can briefly alter how fallback policies are evaluated (we do a quick sync of region capacity tables). If some router nodes had old tables and others new, you get split-brain routing decisions.

Jen C: Recommend we do two things immediately:
  - Correlate customer request-ids with router node ids in our logs around 14:12–14:20.
  - Check router-v2 rollout health and any 5xxs/connection errors between router and regional pools.

Maya R: I'm pulling logs now. Customer provided request ids: [req_0a8f3b9c, req_0a8f3b9d, req_0a8f3b9f]. I'll paste them when I have raw logs.

support-bot: FYI — infra alert: router-v2 rollout droll-927 reported 2% increased 502s at 14:14:50 UTC

Maya R: Logs (scrubbed) — sample correlation:

```
2026-11-04T14:12:07Z router-node-03 req=req_0a8f3b9c action=route src_region=eu-west-1 dst_region=eu-west-1 decision=accept
2026-11-04T14:12:07Z router-node-07 req=req_0a8f3b9d action=route src_region=eu-west-1 dst_region=us-west-2 decision=fallback-enqueue
2026-11-04T14:12:07Z router-node-07 req=req_0a8f3b9d dst_pool=us-west-2 result=throttle code=egress_guard
2026-11-04T14:16:02Z router-node-02 req=req_0a8f3b9f action=route src_region=eu-west-1 dst_region=us-west-2 decision=accept
```

Kai: This is gold. Shows mixed behavior across nodes and one explicit `egress_guard` throttle. That suggests two things: (1) us-west-2 pool was at guard limit during some handoffs, (2) router-node-02 got updated later and accepted the route after pool pressure dropped.

Samir P: Root cause hypothesis: overlapping router rollout + sudden customer burst => some requests rerouted to us-west and hit egress guard. When guard rejects, router returns standard 429 with rate-limit headers instead of a distinct fallback header in older code path. We should patch router to always emit `x-rw-fallback-throttle` for these cases.

Jen C: Prioritization: P1 for engineering (router tweak) or P2? Customer impact: intermittent 429s causing user-facing failures but not complete outage.

Kai: I'd call it P1 for a hotfix on header consistency because support can't easily distinguish fallback throttles from client-side quota exhaustion in current UX. Also add an ops play to pause rollouts on elevated cross-region traffic.

Maya R: Customer asked for short-term mitigation — can we increase cross-region guard threshold for acct-level? Any per-customer bypass?

Samir P: We have an emergency knob: `router.fallback_override` but it's global and requires signoff. Ops can lift it for 10 minutes to let fallback succeed, but we need to coordinate with SRE due to cost and tail risk.

Jen C: I'll open an internal ticket on infra: INF-5298 (router: ensure fallback throttle header + rollout gating). For now, Ops, can you check if we can do a targeted override for acme-ops?

Kai: Ops: please check `router.metrics.fallback_guard[us-west-2]` and the override state. If we need to apply, do a staged increase and monitor `pool_latency` and `queue_length`.

deploy-bot: rollout droll-927: pause requested by eng-sre at Thu Nov 04 14:17:03 UTC — status=paused

Samir P: Great. Next steps summary for support to reply to customer:
  - Explain root cause: their burst outran regional capacity and overlapping router rollout caused some requests to be routed to a region that was guarded => intermittent 429s.
  - Offer scheduled window with us to run controlled burst while we hold rollouts and optionally apply fallback override.
  - Ask for their header/req-id dumps (we need all request ids from the run).

Maya R: I'm drafting the reply now. Will include suggestion: run lower-concurrency repro (100c) while we pause rollouts, then escalate for override if that still fails.

Jen C: Add note: if customer is on Dedicated plan, we should offer reserved cross-region bump temporarily (billing team needs to sign off).

Maya R: Thanks all. I'll attach logs and ticket INF-5298 to the thread and follow up once ops confirms override status.

Kai: After hotfix, we should also add a postmortem checklist: (1) router rollout gating when cross-region traffic > 20% of pool capacity, (2) consistent headers for fallback throttles, (3) better doc for customers about multi-region failover semantics.

Samir P: Agreed. Closing loop: once customer confirms green on the controlled run, we can consider incident resolved.

Maya R: Customer scheduled the test for 14:50 UTC. I'll update after test.

support-bot: reminder set for 14:51 UTC to check test results :alarm_clock:

Maya R: thanks — thread closed for now until test completes.
